verdict.rationale: Notte documents an `observe()` call (and CLI `notte page observe`) that returns element IDs and selectors for page interaction. It also pitches a hybrid scripting-plus-AI model and says 'no selectors, no maintenance', which implies DOM-understanding primitives that tolerate page changes. However, the evidence never shows explicit act/click/type calls on natural-language-described elements, and the 'no selectors' claim applies to whole-task prompting rather than per-action primitives. Missing for 10: documented act/click/type primitives that take element descriptions, evidence that actions survive selector or layout changes, and independent hands-on corroboration.
